title: Louisiana: history overview
d: Louisiana: the Pelican State, admitted 1812 (18th); capital Baton Rouge.
definition: Louisiana: the Pelican State, admitted 1812 (18th); capital Baton Rouge.
description: Louisiana — "Pelican State" — entered the Union 1812 (18th). Its capital is Baton Rouge and its largest city is New Orleans. French and Spanish colony. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Louisiana achieved statehood 1812 (18th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Louisiana Purchase 1803. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Louisiana its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Louisiana went from territory to state.
definition: How Louisiana went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Louisiana: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Civil War; Huey Long era. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Louisiana's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Baton Rouge
d: Baton Rouge is the capital of Louisiana.
definition: Baton Rouge is the capital of Louisiana.
description: Baton Rouge has been the seat of Louisiana government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Louisiana's largest is New Orleans — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Pelican State
description: The nickname "Pelican State" captures how Louisiana sees itself — and how America sees it. Oil, jazz, Katrina 2005. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Union, justice, confidence."

title: Motto: Union, justice, confidence
d: The state motto of Louisiana is "Union, justice, confidence."
definition: The state motto of Louisiana is "Union, justice, confidence."
description: The motto "Union, justice, confidence" is Louisiana's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Pelican with chicks on blue; gold fringe. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
